sources.entry: OpenTerminal - App for macOS that opens a new Finder window and changes the current directory to the folder launched by the app.

summary.one_liner: A small macOS app that opens a Terminal (or iTerm2) window at the folder currently shown in Finder, launchable from the Finder toolbar or Dock.
summary.what_it_does: Opens a new Terminal window whose current directory is set to the folder shown in the active Finder window. If one or more folders are selected in Finder, each selected folder opens in its own Terminal window. Clicking it with no selection opens Terminal at the Finder window's path. Launched directly, it opens Terminal at the app's bundle path. The README says the target can be switched from Apple Terminal to iTerm2 via a macOS defaults write command, and back again with defaults remove. The app is built from source with xcodebuild.
use_cases: Open a terminal in the folder I'm viewing in Finder
Add a terminal shortcut to the Finder toolbar
Open several selected Finder folders in separate terminal windows
Use iTerm2 instead of Terminal from Finder
Launch a terminal from the Dock on macOS
how_to_run: Move the built OpenTerminal.app (in build/Release) to a folder, then drag it with ⌘+⌥ onto a Finder window toolbar
Optional: defaults write jp.ez-style.appid.OpenTerminal ESTargetTerminalBundleIdentifier "com.googlecode.iterm2" to target iTerm2
Optional: defaults remove jp.ez-style.appid.OpenTerminal ESTargetTerminalBundleIdentifier to return to Terminal
notable: Finder toolbar integration: click the app icon to open Terminal at the current Finder folder
Multi-selection support: each selected folder opens in its own Terminal window
Switchable target between Apple Terminal and iTerm2 via a defaults setting
Built from source with a single xcodebuild command
caveats: Requires Xcode and building from source; the README gives no prebuilt download
Switching to iTerm2 prompts for AppleScript to select the iTerm2 application
